title: Short-stay departure-to-arrival turnover planning
audience: Short-stay turnover cleaners and coordinators planning a turnover between guests.
learningOutcomes: Confirm the turnover window and permission to enter before going in.
Plan the tasks by their dependencies, including laundry and drying time.
Control the deadline without shortcuts, and escalate where time or access is short.

instruction.heading: Confirm the window and the access
instruction.body: Before you travel to the property, read the booking handover, the departure confirmation, the next arrival deadline, the property checklist and the access instructions. Compare them. If the departure time, the arrival time or the access code differ between documents, report the conflict to the coordinator before you go in, and do not resolve it by guessing. Never assume that a guest has left because the checkout time has passed. A guest who is still inside is a stop point, not a reason to enter. Confirm in writing, through the channel your business uses, that you have permission to enter, and record the time that permission was confirmed. Permission comes from the booking terms and from the property manager or owner's instructions, so it is the coordinator's job to hold that confirmation and pass it to you.

instruction.heading: Plan by dependency
instruction.body: Work out which tasks must happen first, because other tasks wait for them. In a typical turnover, access verification and the safety scan come first, then rubbish removal and linen collection. Starting an approved laundry cycle is the task that often sets the finish time, because the cycle, the drying and the return of clean linen all have to happen before the beds are made. Bathroom and kitchen products may need a contact time before they are wiped, and that time must be built in rather than cut short. Keep the clean supplies separate from the used linen so that the two never cross. Allow for the final inspection and any reinspection before you plan the release time. The arithmetic is simple: a laundry cycle that runs for, example, three hours and then needs drying time cannot finish inside a two-hour window, however fast the cleaning is.

instruction.heading: The time budget, the buffer and escalation
instruction.body: Build a time budget for each zone, with a final inspection buffer. As an example only, a plan might give a two-bedroom unit a set time for each zone and hold back a fixed share of the total as a buffer for the inspection. The figures for your business come from the coordinator's standard, not from this lesson. If the time is not enough, tell the coordinator early, not at the end. Prioritise safety checks and mandatory hygiene tasks, and seek an authorised schedule change rather than cutting steps. Record the start and finish times, the reason for any delay, and the person you told. If a guest is still inside after checkout, contact the coordinator, revise the task order, and record the delay. Do not enter, and do not pressure the guest to leave. Do not omit contact times, do not conceal defects, and do not certify a room you have not inspected.

procedure: Read the booking handover, departure confirmation, arrival deadline, property checklist and access instructions, and check that they agree.
Confirm permission to enter in writing, and record the time it was confirmed.
Sequence the dependent tasks first, including the laundry cycle, drying and the contact times for cleaning products.
Set a time budget for each zone, and hold a final inspection buffer.
If time is short, or a guest is still present, tell the coordinator early and seek an authorised schedule change.
Log the start, finish, zones cleaned, supplies used, defects, lost property and any areas you could not access.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner arrives 20 minutes after the scheduled checkout time to find a guest still inside, with a new arrival due in three hours.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and what changes in the plan?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not enter, and do not pressure the guest. Contact the coordinator with the time of arrival and the arrival deadline. Do not start the turnover until permission to enter is confirmed. Ask the coordinator to revise the order: if the guest leaves late, the laundry and the cleaning of the bathrooms may need to move to the time after the guest has gone. Record the delay, the time you contacted the coordinator, and the revised plan.

workedExamples.situation: The arrival time for the next guest has moved forward by an hour after you have started the laundry cycle.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you protect the deadline without cutting steps?
workedExamples.reasoning: Tell the coordinator at once, with the time remaining and the tasks still to do. Check which tasks can run at the same time, for example the bathroom contact time while the laundry runs, without skipping any step. If the mandatory tasks cannot fit, ask for an authorised schedule change or extra support. Record the change in the turnover log.

equipmentAndPpe: Property checklist and access instructions, checked against the booking handover before travel.
A timer or the time budget sheet for each zone.
Gloves and other PPE as the product SDS and the business procedure set for the products used.
A way to contact the coordinator, and the escalation contact set for the business.
Turnover log to record start and finish times, delays and permission confirmations.

commonErrors.error: Entering because checkout time has passed.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the departure and your permission to enter first, and treat a guest still inside as a stop point.

commonErrors.error: Skipping contact times to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the contact times into the time budget, and escalate early if the budget does not fit.

commonErrors.error: Planning the laundry as if it finishes in the same time as the cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Sequence the laundry and drying first, and check that the finish time still fits.

commonErrors.error: Certifying a room that was not inspected.
commonErrors.prevention: Certify only what was inspected, and list anything else as not inspected.

commonErrors.error: Not logging a delay, so the coordinator cannot see why the schedule moved.
commonErrors.prevention: Log every delay with the time, the reason and the person told.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Entry and privacy. Permission to enter comes from the booking terms and the property manager's or owner's rules, and the coordinator holds it.

Chemicals. Products must be used under the label and the SDS, and the SDS must be easy for the worker who uses the product to reach. The hazardous chemicals register applies to hazardous chemicals used at a workplace.

Host and letting-agent duties. Registration of a short-term rental, short-stay limits and any host obligations are duties of the host or letting agent, not of the cleaner. This lesson does not describe those duties, and the coordinator should confirm them for the property.

The turnover plan, time budget and buffer are business practice. The figures in the worked examples are examples only, and the business's own standard applies. This lesson does not set a legal cleaning time.

qualityStandard: Booking window and permission to enter confirmed and recorded before entry in the simulated turnover.
Dependent tasks sequenced, with the laundry, drying and contact times allowed for.
A final inspection buffer included in the time budget.
Any delay escalated to the coordinator and recorded in the case study.
documentationEvidence: Turnover log with start, finish, zones, supplies, defects, lost property and inaccessible areas.
Record of the permission to enter, with the time it was confirmed.
Delay and schedule-change record, with the person told and the revised plan.
summary: Confirm the window and permission before you enter, and treat a guest still inside as a stop point.
Plan by dependency, and allow for laundry, drying and contact times.

knowledgeChecks.question: Can you enter a short-stay property because checkout time has passed?
options: Yes, always, since the guest is gone and the time has passed
No, confirm the departure and your permission to enter first
Yes, if the door is open when you arrive at the property

knowledgeChecks.question: Time is short for a turnover. What is the correct response?
options: Skip the contact times and go straight to the next room
Certify the rooms anyway and sign the checklist today before the guest arrives
Tell the coordinator early and seek an authorised schedule change

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the laundry often set the finish time of a turnover?
options: Because the laundry cycle and drying must finish before the clean linen can be made up
Because laundry is always the last task of the day in every single turnover
Because laundry looks better when it is done early in the day for the guest
